blocks.prompt: 9 Solve the following trigonometric equation: \(\sin 2x - \sqrt{3}\cos x = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
The angles are different (\(2x\) and \(x\)): use \(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\) so that only \(x\) appears.
Then \(\cos x\) is a common factor.
Plan: solve \(\cos x = 0\) and \(\sin x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\); write all families.
steps:
Given: \(\sin 2x - \sqrt{3}\cos x = 0\).
To find: principal solutions and general solution.
Method: double-angle formula, then factorise.

Use the double-angle formula
\[2\sin x\cos x - \sqrt{3}\cos x = 0\]
Why: \(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\) makes every term an expression in the same angle \(x\).

Factorise
\[\cos x\left(2\sin x - \sqrt{3}\right) = 0\]
\[\cos x = 0\ \text{ or }\ \sin x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Why: \(\cos x\) is common; a product is zero only when a factor is zero.

When \(\cos x = 0\)
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\]
in \([0, 2\pi]\). These differ by \(\pi\), so in general \(x = \frac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\).
Why: cosine is zero at the top and bottom of the unit circle.

When \(\sin x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)
Sine is positive: quadrants I and II, reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\).
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
\[x = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\]
Why: \(\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

General solution
\[\left\{\dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{2\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Why: union of the families of both factors; sine repeats after \(2\pi\).
blocks.final_answer: Principal solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\): \(x = \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{2\pi}{3}, \frac{3\pi}{2}\). General solution: \(\left\{\frac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\right\}\) \(\cup\) \(\left\{\frac{\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\}\) \(\cup\) \(\left\{\frac{2\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

Every answer on this page is ours: worked out step by step, checked independently with a computer algebra system (sympy) and compared with a solution book. As in the book's examples, we give the principal solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution as a union of sets.
